phil-mind-01-c2.text: Leopold Stubenberg (2005). Neutral Monism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-mind-01-c2.quote: both mind and matter are composed of a neutral-stuff which, in isolation, is neither mental nor material
phil-mind-01-c2.claim: Neutral monism (Russell, Spinoza in a different form) holds that the fundamental substance is neither mental nor physical.

phil-mind-01-c3.text: William Robinson (1999). Epiphenomenalism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-mind-01-c3.quote: compared mental events to a steam whistle that contributes nothing to the work of a locomotive.
phil-mind-01-c3.claim: Epiphenomenalism (Huxley) is the view that mental events are byproducts of physical brain events but have no causal power.
